rpc.tournament.admin_dashboard.description: Permission: any of workspace `tournament.read`, `team.read`, `match.read`, `user.read` or `achievement.read`. Returns the organizer home of one workspace: one card per tournament that is not finished (hidden ones included) plus completed tournaments within 14 days of finishing whose wrap-up (results confirmed, duel logs, achievements, standings) is not done; the next 7 days of phase-schedule boundaries plus every overdue phase start; the work queue of those cards ordered by severity; and the backlog of every other tournament with a data-quality issue. Each field group is null when the caller lacks the permission that gates it, never zero. 422 without `workspace_id`, 403 without any of the permissions.

rpc.tournament.admin_dashboard_trends.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.read`. Returns participants, newcomers, duel log coverage and the median match-end-to-confirmation time of the workspace's last 10 finished, non-league, non-hidden tournaments, oldest first, optionally narrowed to one installed `discipline` (404 `discipline_not_installed` for an unknown code). 422 without `workspace_id`.

schema.description: Installed discipline code; absent or "all": every game

rpc.tournament.admin_encounter_readiness.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Sets one participation's captain readiness (body `{encounter_team_id, ready}`) for an organizer starting a match whose captain is unreachable, and answers `{readiness}` keyed by participation. Signals the room (`encounter:{id}:map-veto`) exactly as the captain's own ready does, so the other captains' screens move without a reload. 404 for an unknown encounter, 409 for a preview bracket's encounter, and 409 on `ready: false` once a pick-ban session of either kind exists — readiness gates session CREATION only, so clearing it afterwards would change nothing; reset the session instead. The readiness row stays unattributed (it names a player identity, which an organizer may not have); the admin audit records who forced it.

rpc.tournament.admin_encounter_reports_l.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the workspace named by `workspace_id`. Every encounter in the workspace with the pair of captain reports filed against it. The row is the encounter, not the report, because a dispute spans two reports and the action that settles it is per-encounter. `scores_match` is null until both sides have reported — that is a different state from disagreeing. `series_score_valid` is advisory: reports predate per-round best-of, so a mismatch is information, not an error. Filter with `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `result_status`, `mismatch_only`, `reported_count` and a free-text `query` over team and encounter names.

rpc.tournament.admin_encounter_reports_s.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the workspace named by `workspace_id`. Counts behind the list's filter chips. Scoped by `tournament_id`, `stage_id` and `query`, but deliberately NOT by the chip filters themselves — each chip reports how many rows it would select, so selecting one does not zero the others.

rpc.tournament.admin_encounter_technical.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Ends the encounter against `loser_team_id` (a participation, never a side) without playing it out, in one transaction: every live pick-ban session is cancelled, every position that is not already CONFIRMED is cancelled, and the result is confirmed (same shape `encounter_set_result` returns). Omit `results` and the scores are derived — the winner takes `best_of // 2 + 1` wins or more if it already had them, the forfeiting participation keeps the maps it really won, capped one short of winning (a Bo5 standing 2:0 for the participation that forfeits is recorded 2:3). Explicit `results` must put the forfeiting participation below every other (422). Same guards as the result route: 409 on a preview bracket's encounter, on a result a later stage already consumed, and on an already confirmed result. `reason` is mandatory — a walkover is never anonymous.

rpc.tournament.admin_game_result.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Writes one series position's numbers as an `admin` result — one `results` line per live participation (`encounter_team_id`, optional score, placement and `column_values`) — and journals the mandatory `reason`; this is the only way a `confirmed` game (locked against captains with 409 `result_locked`) ever changes. When the room's result rotation (`result_*` first-ban rotation) opened the next round off this position and the correction changes who opens it, that round is scrapped and re-opened for the corrected opener in the same commit — provided nobody used it yet; 409 `dependent_round_started` (nothing written, no audit row) when it was already used: a submission on one of its steps, or its game given a side, claimed or confirmed. The way out is to undo that round (captains) or reset the room first. The response is `{game, reset_downstream}`. Also 409 `side_pick_pending` while the position's side step is open, 409 `side_pick_required` while a room that picks this game's sides left them incomplete, 409 `map_not_selected` while the position still has no map (an organizer names it through the pick-ban or the captain map choice first), and 404 when the game belongs to another encounter or is cancelled. When the encounter is confirmed after the correction and linked to a Challonge match, the corrected result is queued for the push to Challonge.

rpc.tournament.admin_match_get.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the workspace named by `workspace_id`. One parsed map with the aggregates the list omits: the round count and how many statistics, kill-feed and event rows were written for it. Returns 404 both for an unknown match and for one outside the workspace named by `workspace_id`, so it cannot be used to probe for ids in another workspace.

rpc.tournament.admin_match_import.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Same request and refusals as the captain submission.
rpc.tournament.admin_match_import.summary: Import a game's match by its external id (organizer)

rpc.tournament.admin_match_imports.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the encounter's workspace. The game's import requests, newest first, each with its organizer `warnings`, derived on read: `fetch_failed` (the request gave up; `last_error` says why), `participants_dropped` (`count` players fewer than the tournament format's starters were observed on the game's teams, e.g. anonymous accounts the decoder dropped) and `banned_character_played` (`characters` the observation shows that this game's hero room banned). Warnings never change a result.
rpc.tournament.admin_match_imports.summary: List a game's match imports with warnings (organizer)

rpc.tournament.admin_matches_list.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the workspace named by `workspace_id`. Every observed duel map across the workspace, not one encounter: every game's, or only the optional `discipline`'s (422 for an unknown code); each row names its own `discipline`. Scores follow the bound game's historical slots; official game results are unchanged. `log_record` is its native ingest job and is null for observations with no raw provenance. Filter with `tournament_id`, `encounter_id`, `map_id`, `log_status`, `unlinked_only` and a free-text `query` over the actual ingest filename and team names. An empty `log_status` filters nothing, so observations without an ingest job stay visible.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_act.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Performs one ban, pick or protect on behalf of the given side (admin override of the captain flow) against the current OPEN step, optionally naming the opponent roster player a per-player ban is spent on, and returns the full room state with nothing hidden. 400 when the current step is blind — use admin_pick_ban_submit for those. On a mix's member pick `member_id` names the member the hero is for (422 on a tournament match).

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_cancel.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Retires one kind's session (body `{kind, reason}`) as CANCELLED and clears any pause, for a room whose veto cannot be played out. A cancelled HERO session simply stops opening rounds; a cancelled MAP session hands the series back to FREEPLAY — the maps it already settled keep their positions and every later one is named by the captains through `captain_select_game_map`. The way back is the session reset. 409 when no session of that kind exists or it is already cancelled.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_config_del.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the workspace of the config's tournament. Deletes a pick-ban config by id (running sessions keep their snapshot).

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_config_lis.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the tournament's workspace (this read is gated on the write action, like its sibling config writes). Returns all pick-ban configs of a tournament for both kinds (map, hero), cascade levels ordered kind, stage, round.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_config_ups.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the tournament's workspace. Creates or replaces the pick-ban config for one (kind, tournament, stage or stage+round) cascade level after validating the ruleset document and the item pool. A ruleset with validation errors is a 422 whose `details.fields[0]` carries `code: "ruleset_invalid"` plus an `issues` array of `{path, code, severity, message}` — the same issue objects admin_pick_ban_rules_validate returns — so the constructor can highlight the offending fields. A hero config whose ruleset holds a `side_pick` step but whose pool is empty is a 422 `pool_required` (save the champion pool first: a pool-less room never opens, yet its side step would hold the result of every game); a pool item that is not a catalog row of the game of the tournament and of the catalog of the kind is a 422 `pool_item_not_in_catalog`. A map config of a game that declares the `mode` kind may also name its modes in the flat `item_ids` (never in slots): ingested logs of another mode are then refused (`mode_not_in_pool`), maps are checked against the map items alone, and the room vetoes the map items only (a pool of only modes opens no room, like a rules template).

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_elect_open.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Names who opens the round a `result_loser_choice` rotation is holding and appends it, on behalf of a losing captain who is unreachable; returns the new room state.
rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_elect_open.summary: Elect a round's opener for a side

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_extend.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Adds `seconds` (10..3600) to the open step's clock by moving its start forward, and returns the room state. Allowed while paused. 409 when no session of that kind is active or the open step has no timer (an untimed or already settled step has nothing to extend).

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_pause.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Freezes (`{kind, paused: true}`) or releases one kind's room and returns its state. A paused session has no deadline at all: the open step's timer stops, nothing auto-resolves, reveals or times out, and every CAPTAIN write (act, submit, dispute, undo, elect-opener) answers 409 `Pick-ban session is paused` while the admin overrides keep working. Resuming gives the step back exactly the time it had left; a step that opened during the pause gets its full timer. Idempotent, and 409 when no session of that kind exists or it is not active.
rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_pause.summary: Pause or resume a pick-ban session

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_reopen.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Voids the last fully revealed step's submissions and re-opens it for a fresh attempt — the organizer's version of a captain dispute, with no attempt budget and no `dispute.enabled` requirement. A reopened open (non-blind) step starts with an empty draft, the voided items available again, so its captain answers it afresh; a blind step's new drafts are prefilled with each side's previous items (still private until everyone locks). A reopened `side_pick` also takes back that game's sides and un-binds the round's side-bound steps, so the re-choice binds them afresh. Returns the new room state. 400 when there is no revealed step to reopen or a later step has already been acted in; 409 `side_locked` when the step is a `side_pick` whose game already has a claim or a confirmed result.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_rules_prev.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the tournament's workspace (gated like the upsert it precedes). Resolves every map of a best-of series against a candidate ruleset and the pool it would be played out of, returning per map the resolved steps, the new and cumulative active ban counts, and (hero kind) the fewest items that can be left per group — the answer to "how many supports survive map 5" before a tournament runs on the rules.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_rules_vali.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the tournament's workspace (gated like the upsert it precedes). Runs the ruleset engine over a candidate document for the given `kind`/`mode` and returns `{valid, issues}`; unlike the upsert it never errors on a bad ruleset — warnings ride along with the errors and only errors clear `valid`.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_session_re.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Drops an encounter's pick-ban session (map or hero, per the body's `kind`) and its entries, re-creates them with freshly resolved seeds and returns the new room state.

rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_submit.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace; on a mix match, its host or a co-host (or a superuser). Replaces one side's draft on a BLIND step on behalf of an absent captain and, with `lock: true`, locks it; every side locked reveals the step. Returns the full room state with nothing hidden. 400 when the current step is not blind, when the side already locked, or when the items break the step's rules.
rpc.tournament.admin_pick_ban_submit.summary: Submit a blind draft for a side

rpc.tournament.admin_pregame_room_histor.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the encounter's workspace. One room's whole story, newest first: the pre-game journal (readiness, session opened/reset/completed, rounds, every captain and organizer action, step reveals, timeouts, disputes, undo, map and series reports, pause/extend/cancel/technical loss) merged with the encounter's result audit (confirm, reopen, auto_confirm, auto_dispute, auto_pending, import, cascade_reset, game_confirm, game_correct, game_cancel). Each entry carries `id` (`room:<id>`/`result:<id>`), `at`, `origin`, `action`, `kind`, `source` (`captain`/`admin`/`system`), `side`, `actor_auth_user_id`, `actor_name` (null for machine actors), `reason` and an action-specific `data` object. Query `limit` is clamped to 1..500, default 200. The journal is keyed by ENCOUNTER, so resetting a session never erases what it did.

schema.description: Page size, clamped to 1..500, default 200.

rpc.tournament.admin_pregame_rooms.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the tournament's workspace. The organizer's board of every pre-game room of a tournament: one row per non-FFA encounter that resolves to a pooled pick-ban config or already has a session, carrying readiness, the map and hero session summaries (open step, acting sides, deadline), the series' game counts, a single `phase` (`teams_unknown`/`readiness`/`map`/`hero`/`report`/`done`/`idle`) and the `attention` flags staff act on (`game_disputed`, `result_disputed`, `awaiting_choice`, `overdue`, `late_not_ready`). Strictly read-only, unlike the room's own state read: it never creates a session, opens a position or settles an expired step, and it answers the whole tournament in a constant number of queries. Rows are ordered stage, round, encounter id; preview-bracket encounters with no session are omitted.

rpc.tournament.captain_match_import.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's live teams (403 otherwise). Body `{external_id}`: the game's match as its discipline's source names it. The stats service fetches it, retrying with backoff for 24 h while the source does not serve it yet, then stores it like an uploaded log and ingests it as evidence for this game (binding, `logs_official` and evidence rules unchanged). Returns the request `{id, status (pending|done|failed), attempts, last_error, external_id, created_at, warnings}`; re-submitting the same id for the same game returns it, a failed one restarts. 422 `unsupported_ingestor` when the encounter's discipline has no match source, 422 `invalid_external_id`, 422 `match_import_tournament_only` outside tournaments (mix, scrim), 404 when the game belongs to another encounter or is cancelled, 409 `match_already_imported` when another game of the workspace holds the same match, 503 when the stats service is unreachable.
rpc.tournament.captain_match_import.summary: Import a game's match by its external id

rpc.tournament.captain_match_imports.description: Permission: authenticated captain of one of the encounter's live teams. The game's import requests, newest first, shaped like the submit's answer; `warnings` is always empty on this read.

rpc.tournament.captain_my_role.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the answer is only about the caller's own captaincy. Returns the calling user's participation for an encounter as `{encounter_team_id, slot}`, both null if they captain none of its seats.

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_act.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams (403 otherwise). Applies one ban, pick or protect to the encounter's live pick/ban session of the given `kind`, under the session's row lock, and returns the caller's new room state. OPEN steps only: a blind step is a 400 that says to use the submit route. Acting when the caller's side does not owe the current step, sending the wrong action for it, naming an item the step's rules do not allow, or omitting the opponent player a per-player ban must name is a 400, as is a session that is not initialized or no longer active. On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown). On a mix match's member pick (spec §11.6) the body names `member_id`, the `encounter.team_member` seat the hero is for: the member themselves or their team's captain may pick (403 otherwise; 422 on a tournament match). An assignment step is answered through captain_pick_ban_submit.

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_dispute.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams (403 otherwise). Unilateral, no opponent consent: voids the last fully revealed BLIND step and re-opens it for a fresh attempt with each side's previous items prefilled, so a captain who named the wrong opponent player can redo it. Allowed only while that step's `dispute` is enabled, its attempt budget is not spent, no later step has been acted in, and the map that round settled has no result yet; anything else is a 400. Returns the caller's new room state. On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown).

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_elect_op.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams, and only the side that LOST the previous round may choose (403 otherwise). Resolves a round the `result_loser_choice` rotation is holding by naming which side opens it, then appends that round and returns the session. 400 when no round is awaiting a choice. An organizer overrides an unreachable captain through admin_pick_ban_elect_opener. On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown).

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_state.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — gated only by the tournament's visibility rule; a mix match's room is public. Returns the live pick/ban room for an encounter and the `kind` path segment ('map' or 'hero', 422 otherwise): the resolved steps, the candidate pool, which sides still owe the current step, both sides' readiness, any open undo request, and for maps the captains' per-map result claims. A captain additionally gets their own side annotated, their eligible items, why their draft cannot be locked yet, and their own unrevealed draft — a blind step never serializes the other side's. When no session can exist yet the payload names why (teams unknown, bracket still a preview, no pick-ban configured, slot count mismatch, sides not ready, waiting on the map round) instead of erroring. A mix room also lists `members` (seats in pick order), the member step's `acting_member_ids`, whom the viewer may pick for (`viewer_member_ids`; a member owes their own pick, a captain also their team's) and each member's choosable heroes (`member_eligible`, Fearless applied).

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_submit.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams (403 otherwise). Replaces the caller's whole draft for the current BLIND step and, with `lock: true`, locks it — a locked submission is final, and once every acting side has locked the step reveals for both. Returns the caller's new room state; while the step is unrevealed it carries the caller's own items and only the opponent's progress counts. 400 when the current step is not blind, when the caller already locked, or when the items break the step's rules (the reasons are also listed in the state's `draft_issues`). On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown). It also answers a mix's assignment step (open, not blind): each item names `member_id`, one hero of the team's picks per member, none a member's Fearless excludes (422 on a tournament match).

rpc.tournament.captain_pick_ban_undo.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams (403 otherwise). Records the calling captain's consent to undo the session's last action and applies it the moment the opposing captain consents too; `consent=false` withdraws an open request (either side may). An applied undo of a `side_pick` takes that game's sides back. Returns the resulting undo block. 400 when the session is not initialized or cancelled, when there is nothing left to undo, or when the target is a map pick whose hero round has already started -- undo those hero actions first; 409 `side_locked` when the undo would take back a side whose game already has a claim or a confirmed result. On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown).

rpc.tournament.captain_ready.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's live participations (403 when the account captains none of them or has no linked player profile). Marks the calling captain's seat ready to begin the encounter's pre-game phase and returns the resulting readiness map, keyed by participation id; idempotent. The pick/ban session only opens once every seat is ready, and any change of team assignment clears them all. On a mix match the captain is the roster snapshot's (the lineup's crown).

rpc.tournament.captain_report_game.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's live participations (403 otherwise). Files the calling captain's own claim of ONE series position's result, immediately after that game rather than at series end: `basis_version` plus one `results` line per participation (`encounter_team_id`, optional score, placement and the stage's own `column_values`). The claiming seat is taken from the caller, never from the body. Every live participation claims independently: matching claims accept the game's result and open whatever the series owes next, differing ones mark the game `disputed` for an organizer. Returns `{disputed, resolved, game}`. 404 when the game belongs to another encounter or is cancelled, 409 `result_locked` once the game is confirmed (only the admin correction changes it), 409 `map_not_selected` while the position still has no map (choose it first, through captain_select_game_map or the map pick-ban), 409 `side_pick_pending` while the position's side step is open, 409 `side_pick_required` while a room that picks this game's sides left them incomplete, 409 on a `basis_version` behind the game's current one, and 409 while the stage bracket is still a preview the organizer has not activated.

rpc.tournament.captain_reports.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — visible to anyone who may view the tournament. Returns every participation's report for an encounter (score, closeness, comment and custom field values), every participation's per-position replay codes under `replay_codes`, and the tournament's match-report form config under `form`, so the report dialog renders exactly the rules the submit endpoint enforces.

rpc.tournament.captain_select_game_map.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's two teams (403 otherwise). Freeplay's half of what the map pick-ban does automatically: names the map an open position is played on, moving a `planned` game to `awaiting_result`. Returns `{game}`. 404 when the game belongs to another encounter, 409 `result_locked` when the position's result is already settled, 409 `side_pick_pending` / `side_pick_required` while the position's sides are not decided where the room picks them, and 409 `map_locked` once a captain has claimed a score against the current map.

rpc.tournament.captain_submit_report.description: Permission: authenticated user who captains one of the encounter's live participations (403 otherwise). Lets a captain submit their own report of the finished series: `basis_version`, `games_played` and one `results` line per live participation (`encounter_team_id`, score and optionally placement or wins — never a side), plus whatever the tournament's match-report form enables — closeness 1..10, per-map match codes, a free-text comment and any organizer-defined text fields. The reporting seat is resolved from the caller, never taken from the body. Fields the config disables are dropped rather than rejected, so a stale client cannot fail a submit; fields it marks required are enforced with a 422. A `basis_version` behind the encounter's current one is stale and refused rather than silently winning. Reports are per-participation; when every live participation's numbers agree the encounter auto-confirms and closeness becomes their average (null when any of them left it blank), otherwise it is disputed — comments and custom values never take part in that comparison. Upsert allowed until confirmed.

rpc.tournament.challonge_create_tourname.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.create` on the target workspace. Creates a tournament from an existing Challonge bracket -- fetches it for the name/description, links it, and imports its current structure and results in one shot. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_export.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.update` on the tournament's workspace. Exports a tournament's bracket to Challonge. 404 when the tournament does not exist, 422 when it has no Challonge source, 409 while an import or export of it is already running (the request waits up to 3 s for it). Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request. Metered: a 429 reports `code=rate_limited` with the exceeded limit in `details.limit_name`.

rpc.tournament.challonge_fetch_matches.description: Permission: global `challonge.read`. Fetches a Challonge tournament's matches from the Challonge API. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_fetch_participa.description: Permission: global `challonge.read`. Fetches a Challonge tournament's participants from the Challonge API. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_fetch_tournamen.description: Permission: global `challonge.read`. Fetches a Challonge tournament by slug from the Challonge API. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_import.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.update` on the tournament's workspace. Imports a tournament's bracket from Challonge, optionally as a dry run. A match Challonge did not change writes nothing (no sync-log row, no recompute, no cache invalidation) and counts as skipped; `matches_synced` counts real writes only. 404 when the tournament does not exist, 422 when it has no Challonge source, 409 while an import or export of it is already running (the request waits up to 3 s for it). Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request. Metered: a 429 reports `code=rate_limited` with the exceeded limit in `details.limit_name`.

rpc.tournament.challonge_push_result.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.update` on the encounter's workspace. Pushes a confirmed encounter result to Challonge and returns a status acknowledgment. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_sync_log.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns the tournament's newest Challonge sync-log entries, `limit` of them (default 50, clamped to 1..200). A match a sync found unchanged leaves no entry; `error_message` is `<ExceptionType>: <message>`, never a traceback. Entries older than 30 days are purged daily.

schema.description: Entries to return, clamped to 1..200, default 50.

rpc.tournament.challonge_team_apply.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.update` on the tournament's workspace. Applies Challonge participant-to-team mappings for a tournament. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.challonge_team_preview.description: Permission: workspace `challonge.read` on the tournament's workspace. Previews the mapping of Challonge participants to teams for a tournament before syncing. Challonge failures are real HTTP errors: 404 `challonge_not_found` when Challonge does not know the tournament, 503 `challonge_unavailable` when it is unreachable, times out, rate-limits or fails (5xx), 400 `challonge_error` when it refuses the request.

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_delete.description: Permission: the message's author, or a moderator of the room (workspace staff). Soft-deletes one message and publishes the removal to the room's subscribers. 404 when the id is not a message of this room. Answers `{deleted: true}`.

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_history.description: Permission: optional authentication. Captains of either team and the workspace's staff always read; anybody else reads only while the room's `spectators_can_read` is on, which a pre-game room has OFF by default (captains trade custom-lobby codes there). A hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and its preview allowlist. Returns the messages plus the room settings, the caller's own viewer rights and — for moderators only — the active mutes. `after_id` tails the room; `limit` pages it. A mix match's chat is read and written only by its seated players (role captain or player) and the mix's hosts (staff); everyone else gets 403.

schema.description: Only messages newer than this id (live tail).
Page size, clamped to 1..200, default 50.

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_mute_clear.description: Permission: moderator of the room (workspace staff). Lifts one account's mute in this room, idempotent. Answers `{deleted: true}`.
rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_mute_clear.summary: Unmute an account in the pre-game chat

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_mute_set.description: Permission: moderator of the room (workspace staff). Mutes one account in this room for `minutes` (1..10080), or until lifted when `minutes` is null, with an optional reason. 422 on muting yourself. Returns the mute.
rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_mute_set.summary: Mute an account in the pre-game chat

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_post.description: Permission: authenticated captain of either team, or workspace staff; spectators never write, at any setting. The body is sanitized and capped at 500 characters. 403 with code `chat_muted` while the account is muted in this room, 429 past 10 messages per 10 seconds. Returns the stored message, which is also fanned out to the room's realtime topic.
rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_post.summary: Post to the pre-game room chat

rpc.tournament.encounter_chat_settings.description: Permission: moderator of the room (workspace staff). Opens or closes the room to spectators and returns the stored setting. Closing it also revokes the spectators already subscribed to the room's realtime topic; a no-op toggle emits nothing.

rpc.tournament.encounter_reopen_result.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Un-confirms an encounter so it can be replayed or re-reported, clearing the participations' scores, closeness and confirmation, and cascading through anything the old result advanced. Team reports are kept. `reason` is mandatory — it is what the journal row carries. 409 when there is no recorded result.

rpc.tournament.encounter_result_audit.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the encounter's workspace. Returns every recorded transition of the encounter's result, newest first. A null actor_user_id means a machine actor (Challonge import, bracket cascade).

rpc.tournament.encounter_set_result.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Confirms an encounter result in one transaction: the participations' scores, status, result_status, result_version and the audit row move together. `reason` is mandatory. Each `results` line names an `encounter_team_id` — never a side — with its score and optional placement; leave `results` empty and name `adopt_report_team_id` to take that participation's own report as truth instead, which resolves a dispute in one call. 422 when neither applies, and 422 `not_a_participation` when a line names an `encounter_team_id` that is not a live participation of this encounter. 409 when the result is already confirmed (reopen it first).

rpc.tournament.encounter_swap_slot.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the encounter's workspace. Swaps one of an encounter's team slots with another slot and answers with both encounters' resulting seats, so the bracket re-renders the pair without a refetch.

rpc.tournament.encounter_update_match.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the workspace resolved from the match. Edits the observed score of any participant, addressed by encounter_team_id (422 for a seat the match does not have), and the nullable duration in seconds. The map must equal the bound game's existing map (409 otherwise). Team IDs, source, code, log_name and other unsupported fields are rejected with 422. Official game scores remain unchanged; score and duration changes carry separate native evidence records in the same transaction as the existing recalculation outbox.

rpc.tournament.encounters_insights.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — an explicit tournament_id is visibility-gated against the caller, and an unfiltered read covers publicly visible tournaments only. Takes the encounter list's filters with the status forced to `completed` and returns their analytics: the count, average closeness (0..1) and its histogram in tenths, final score lines, the split by stage kind, the 6 most played maps, the 4 closest encounters, average series length, and — over the duels of more than one map (`multi_map`) — sweeps and series that went the distance.

rpc.tournament.encounters_overview.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — an explicit tournament_id is visibility-gated against the caller, and an unfiltered overview counts publicly visible tournaments only. Takes the encounter list's filters and returns the browse's counts: the status segments (`all`, `live`, `upcoming`, `completed`; the status filter ignored, the toggles applied) and the toggles (`finals`, `upsets`, `with_logs`, `my_team`; every other filter applied, that toggle forced on — `my_team` is 0 without an identity), plus `completed_with_logs`, `recent_completed` (played in the last 7 days) and up to 4 encounters in play.

rpc.tournament.ffa_game_cancel.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Voids one game of a lobby, keeping it as history and freeing its position for a replay. Requires a reason. Answers the lobby's settled table — which may have reopened, since a voided game no longer counts towards the games count; a lobby it reopens retires every seat its old result advanced downstream, as `encounter_reopen_result` does. 409 `ffa_not_a_lobby` when the encounter is a duel rather than a lobby.

rpc.tournament.ffa_game_results_set.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the encounter's workspace. Records one game of a lobby: a line per seated team, every team exactly once, carrying one value per column of the stage. Placements are required when the stage's formula reads the place and derived from the game's points otherwise (ties share a place). Re-recording a confirmed position is a correction and needs a reason. The lobby completes itself when its confirmed games reach its games count, and reopens when they no longer do. Answers the lobby's settled table, with every column on it. 409 when a later stage has already been seeded from this group, and 409 `ffa_not_a_lobby` when the encounter is a duel rather than a lobby.

rpc.tournament.ffa_games_count_set.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the encounter's workspace. Changes how many games THIS lobby plays. Never below the number it has already confirmed (422), since the games are the record. Answers the lobby's settled table, completed or reopened by the new count. A count that completes the lobby runs every effect of a confirmation (the completed event, bracket advance and standings, the Challonge push); one that reopens a confirmed lobby retires every seat its old result advanced downstream. 409 `ffa_not_a_lobby` when the encounter is a duel rather than a lobby.

rpc.tournament.ffa_lobby.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one lobby's table, the same shape the stage read answers per group. 409 `ffa_not_a_lobby` when the encounter is a duel rather than a lobby.

rpc.tournament.ffa_stage.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one lobby table per group of an ffa_league stage, in group order: the stage's scoring rules, every seated team with its running points and column sums, and one cell per planned game. Columns the organizer marked non-public are omitted here entirely — their sums and per-game values never leave the service. Positions come from the group's standings, so a stage nobody has ranked yet answers null positions in seat order.

rpc.tournament.ffa_stage_admin.description: Permission: workspace `match.result` on the tournament's workspace — whoever may record a result may read the values behind it. The same lobby tables as the public stage read, with the columns marked non-public still on them: that is what the result-entry dialog fills in. Not cached by the gateway. 401 without an identity.

rpc.tournament.get_encounter.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one encounter by id with optionally hydrated related entities selected via the entities query param.

rpc.tournament.get_match.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one match by id: its participants (official result lines and observed team facts), every member, segment and fact at every grain, and optionally hydrated related entities, scoped to the given workspace.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.

rpc.tournament.get_match_kill_feed.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one match's whole event timeline in chronological order with the characters its events name, scoped to the given workspace; 404s when the match is outside that scope.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.

rpc.tournament.get_pick_ban_configs.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns the tournament's map pick-ban configs in cascade order.

rpc.tournament.get_stages.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns all stages of a tournament ordered by stage order, with their items and item inputs hydrated.

rpc.tournament.get_standings.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns the standings for a tournament with optionally hydrated related entities selected via the entities query param.

rpc.tournament.get_team.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one team by id with optionally hydrated related entities (players, captain, tournament) selected via the entities query param.

rpc.tournament.get_tournament.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist. Returns one tournament by id with optionally hydrated related entities selected via the entities query param.

rpc.tournament.grid_delete.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.delete` on the grid's workspace. Hard-deletes a division grid and its versions/tiers/mappings (204 no body); refuses the workspace default or grids whose versions are used by tournaments. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_import_job_get.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read` on the job's workspace. Returns durable progress, result, and failure details for one workspace import job. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403).

rpc.tournament.grid_import_jobs_list.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read`. Lists recent workspace import jobs, optionally restricted to pending and running jobs.

rpc.tournament.grid_mapping_get.description: Permission: authenticated user who can see BOTH versions — any authenticated user for a system grid; for a workspace-owned grid, a member of that workspace or a holder of `division_grid.read` there (404 otherwise). Returns the division mapping between a source and target grid version.

rpc.tournament.grid_mapping_put.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update` on the source version's workspace, plus read access to the target version (a member of its workspace or a holder of `division_grid.read` there, or a system grid; 404 otherwise). Creates or updates the division mapping between two grid versions. The mapping belongs to the source version's workspace, so a workspace may map its own versions onto a system version (what activating that system version needs); a mapping from a system version is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`.

rpc.tournament.grid_marketplace_grids.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read` on the target workspace; a hidden source workspace additionally requires membership of it or superuser (404 otherwise). Lists importable division grids from a source workspace.

rpc.tournament.grid_marketplace_import.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create` on the target workspace; a hidden source workspace additionally requires membership of it or superuser (404 otherwise). Creates or reuses an idempotent background import job (202 Accepted). 404 when a selected version is not in the selected grid. The job fails as a conflict (409) when the source's provenance no longer matches or a concurrent import changed this workspace's imports, and as 404 when its source or target workspace is gone; its `error` carries the message. A job still running 15 minutes after it started is requeued.

rpc.tournament.grid_marketplace_prefligh.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create` on the target workspace; a hidden source workspace additionally requires membership of it or superuser (404 otherwise). Reports conflicts, asset policy, operation counts, and a stable source fingerprint without writing data. 404 when a selected version is not in the selected grid.

rpc.tournament.grid_marketplace_workspac.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read` on the target workspace. Lists workspaces whose division grids can be imported into the target workspace.

rpc.tournament.grid_portable_export.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read` on the grid's workspace. Exports every version and slug-based mapping as a portable division-grid/v1 document. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403).

rpc.tournament.grid_portable_import.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create` on the target workspace. Imports a validated division-grid/v1 document in library, sync, or copy mode. Every version in the document is validated before anything is written: 400 with the create-version messages (at least one tier, duplicate slug or sort order, an invalid rank range, more than one open-ended tier).

rpc.tournament.grid_save.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update`. Server-authoritative save: applies cosmetic edits in place, or spawns a new version, auto-generates mappings from every used source version, and auto-activates when complete, but only if the grid already holds the workspace's active version for its game (another grid is activated explicitly). A `grid_id` of another workspace is 404. A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_update.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update` on the grid's workspace, or `division_grid.delete` when the body archives it (`archived: true`). Renames, archives, or restores a workspace-owned division grid. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_activate.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update`. Atomically checks mapping readiness and assigns the published version as the workspace default. 404 for another workspace's version. A system grid's version may be activated: this writes only the workspace's own default, never the system grid.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_clone.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create` on the grid's workspace. Clones a division grid version into a new draft (201 Created). A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_create.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create` on the grid's workspace. Creates a new version of a division grid (201 Created). A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_delete.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.delete` on the grid's workspace. Deletes a division grid version by id (204 no body). A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_get.description: Permission: authenticated user who can see the version: any authenticated user for a system grid (no workspace); for a workspace-owned grid, a member of that workspace or a holder of `division_grid.read` there (superusers pass). 404 for anyone else. Returns one division grid version by id.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_publish.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update` on the grid's workspace. Publishes a division grid version. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_readiness.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read`. Checks that mappings from every version used by workspace tournaments to the target version are complete. 404 for another workspace's version.

rpc.tournament.grid_version_update.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.update` on the grid's workspace. Updates a division grid version by id. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403). A system grid is read-only: a write to it, its versions or tiers is 403 with `details.fields[0].code = division_grid_read_only`, before the permission check.

rpc.tournament.grid_versions_list.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read` on the grid's workspace. Lists the versions of a division grid. A grid, version or job the caller cannot see (another workspace's, unless the caller is a member or holds `division_grid.read` there) is 404, checked before the permission (403).

rpc.tournament.grid_workspace_create.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.create`. Creates a division grid in a workspace. `slug` is optional: when omitted it is derived as `{discipline}-grid`, then `-2`, `-3`… With `from_version_id` (a published version of this workspace's or a system grid of the same game; 404 for another workspace's version, 422 `division_grid_discipline_mismatch` for another game, 409 for an unpublished one) v1 is a published copy of that version's tiers and label; otherwise v1 is the game's native ladder, and a game without one starts with no version. Never activates anything.

rpc.tournament.grid_workspace_list.description: Permission: workspace `division_grid.read`. Lists a workspace's division grids, each with `tournament_count`: the tournaments pinned to any of its versions.

rpc.tournament.job_get.description: Permission: workspace `standing.update` when the job's kind is 'standings', otherwise `stage.update`, on the workspace of the job's tournament. Returns one tournament computation job by id.

rpc.tournament.job_list.description: Permission: workspace `stage.read` on the tournament the query scopes to; listing unscoped (neither `tournament_id` nor `stage_id`) is superuser-only. Lists tournament computation jobs filtered by tournament/stage/active-only with a 1-100 limit.

rpc.tournament.list_encounters.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — an explicit tournament_id filter is visibility-gated against the caller, and an unfiltered page is restricted to publicly visible tournaments. Returns a paginated list of encounters for the search filters, with viewer-scoped fields resolved from the optional identity.

rpc.tournament.list_matches.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — an explicit tournament_id filter is visibility-gated against the caller, and an unfiltered page is restricted to publicly visible tournaments. Returns a paginated list of matches for the search filters within the given workspace.

rpc.tournament.list_teams.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — an explicit tournament_id filter is visibility-gated against the caller, and an unfiltered page is restricted to publicly visible tournaments. Returns a paginated list of teams for the filter params within the given workspace: every game's, or only the optional `discipline`'s (by the team's tournament; 422 for an unknown code). `sort=group` and `sort=placement` paginate like every other sort: teams without a group or placement come last, ties break on team id, and `total` and `only_count` count the same rows.

rpc.tournament.list_tournaments.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — the page is filtered to the tournaments the viewer may see, so hidden ones surface only for their workspace's admins and preview-allowlisted users. Returns a paginated, sortable, searchable list of tournaments. `status` may be repeated (`?status=live&status=playoffs`) and matches any of the values. `per_page=-1` returns every matching row up to 500.

rpc.tournament.lookup_tournaments.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — hidden tournaments, and every tournament of a hidden workspace, are never listed here, for any caller. Returns a lightweight id/name list of up to 500 most-recent tournaments, optionally filtered by workspace, league flag and installed discipline (an uninstalled code is 422), for pickers.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.
Installed discipline code; absent lists every game.

rpc.tournament.pick_ban_outcomes.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist (404 otherwise, and for an unknown tournament). Returns every hero ban of the tournament's encounters an anonymous spectator may see in the room (`hero_bans`: one row per banned hero of a current-attempt submission to a ban step that is revealed or not blind; `first_map` when the step plays round 1, `target_player_id` the opponent roster player a per-player ban is spent on) and every map its map rooms picked or banned (`map_outcomes`). Cached up to 30 seconds: a live room's newest bans may lag that long.

rpc.tournament.pick_ban_rules_catalog.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — the catalog describes the rules ENGINE (which condition leaves and constraints exist, what parameters they take) plus ONE discipline's vocabulary: its item groups per kind (character classes declared by its module, mode slugs for maps) and its presets (the module's own plus the generic map presets; a preset's `first_ban_rotation`, when set, is the rotation the preset needs; `mix_eligible` says whether a pickup mix may play it -- a hero preset that bans no player on map 1 of a Bo1). `discipline` is required: 422 when absent, 404 `discipline_not_installed` for a code no module declares, never another game's presets. The pick-ban constructor loads it before a config exists to attach it to.

schema.description: Explicit discipline code.

rpc.tournament.preview_access_add.description: Permission: workspace `owner`/`admin` role on the tournament's workspace (403 otherwise). Allowlists one account (body `auth_user_id`, 422 when absent) to view a tournament before it is public and invalidates the cached tournament read so the change lands immediately.

rpc.tournament.preview_access_list.description: Permission: workspace `owner`/`admin` role on the tournament's workspace (403 otherwise); no per-resource permission substitutes. Returns every account allowlisted to view a tournament while it is still hidden, as id/tournament_id/auth_user_id/created_at rows.

rpc.tournament.preview_access_remove.description: Permission: workspace `owner`/`admin` role on the tournament's workspace (403 otherwise). Removes an account's preview allowlist entry (204 no body) and invalidates the cached tournament read.

rpc.tournament.reg_approve.description: Permission: workspace `registration.approve` on the registration's workspace. Approves a registration (recording the reviewer) and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_bulk_add_balancer.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the tournament's workspace. Adds multiple registrations to the balancer with a given status, returning updated/skipped counts and broadcasting a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_bulk_approve.description: Permission: workspace `registration.approve` on the tournament's workspace. Approves multiple registrations by id (at most 500 per call), returning approved and skipped ids and broadcasting a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_bulk_set_balancer_sta.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the tournament's workspace. Explicitly pins the balancer status (not_in_balancer / excluded / a custom slug) on multiple registrations, returning updated/skipped counts and broadcasting a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_check_in.description: Permission: workspace `registration.check_in` on the registration's workspace. Checks a registration in or out (per the body flag) and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_create_manual.description: Permission: workspace `registration.create` on the tournament's workspace, plus `registration.approve` when the body's `status` is approved and `registration.reject` when it is rejected or banned. Admin-creates a registration for a tournament (201 Created) and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_delete.description: Permission: workspace `registration.delete` on the registration's workspace. Soft-deletes a registration (204 no body) and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_form_get.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns a tournament's registration form config, or null if none.

rpc.tournament.reg_form_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the tournament's workspace. Creates or replaces a tournament's registration form config (built-in and custom fields).

rpc.tournament.reg_include_balancer.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the registration's workspace. Adds an approved registration to the balancer pool, rated ready/incomplete from its role ranks, and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_list.description: Permission: workspace `registration.read` on the tournament's workspace. Lists a tournament's registrations with status metadata and per-registration OW-rank snapshots, filtered by status/inclusion/source and optionally including deleted.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_check_in.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller's own registration only. Checks the calling user's own registration in, blocking when the form requires a confirmed-public OW profile that is private, or when a required subscription is confirmed missing (an undetermined verdict fails open).

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_create.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller registers only themselves. Lets a user self-register for a tournament (201 Created) after validating the form is open and the input; rejects duplicates with 409, refuses with 400 only when the form's subscription_stage is 'registration' and a required subscription is confirmed missing by an automatic check (a verdict a challenge code could still change is deferred to check-in, and an undetermined verdict fails open). With the default stage 'check_in' sign-up is never refused on a subscription.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_form.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — gated only by the tournament's visibility rule. Returns the public registration form (with sub-role catalog) for a tournament, or null if none.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_get_me.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — resolved from the caller's own token, never from a supplied id. Returns the calling user's registration for a tournament, or null if none.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_list.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — gated only by the tournament's visibility rule. Returns the live public registration list for a tournament with tournament-history and division grids.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_recheck_me.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller's own registration only. Forces a live subscription check and queues a re-fetch of the registration's BattleTags, each only when the tournament requires it; returns 204 and the client refetches its registration. One call per user per 60 seconds: a repeat answers 429 with Retry-After.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_update_me.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller's own registration only. Lets a user update their own still-pending registration after re-validating the input.

rpc.tournament.reg_pub_withdraw_me.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller's own registration only. Withdraws the calling user's own registration and returns the new status; refuses with 409 once the registration has been checked in (only an organizer can withdraw an attendee from that point on).

rpc.tournament.reg_rank_autofill_apply.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` and `registration.roles` on the tournament's workspace. Autofills registration ranks from parsed OW data, persisting changes and broadcasting a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_rank_autofill_preview.description: Permission: workspace `registration.read` on the tournament's workspace. Previews autofilling registration ranks from parsed OW data without writing.

rpc.tournament.reg_reject.description: Permission: workspace `registration.reject` on the registration's workspace. Rejects a registration (recording the reviewer) and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_restore.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the registration's workspace, plus `registration.approve` because a restore lands the registration approved (unless it already is). Restores a withdrawn or rejected registration and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_set_balancer_status.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the registration's workspace. Sets a registration's balancer status and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_update.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the registration's workspace, plus `registration.roles` when the body carries `roles`, an `answers.roles` answer, `pin` or `clear_pin`, and — when the body changes `status` — `registration.approve` to make it approved or `registration.reject` to make it rejected or banned. Updates a registration's profile, roles, and statuses and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.reg_user_rank_history.description: Permission: workspace `registration.read` on the workspace named by the required `workspace_id` query param, checked (403) before any validation error. Returns a user's balancer rank history within that workspace for the installed game named by the required `discipline` query param (422 `discipline_not_installed` otherwise); another game's ranks are never included.

schema.description: Explicit discipline code.

rpc.tournament.reg_withdraw.description: Permission: workspace `registration.update` on the registration's workspace. Withdraws a registration and broadcasts a realtime change.

rpc.tournament.regform_template_apply.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the tournament's workspace. Copies the template's question set onto the tournament's registration form and returns the form. An ordinary schema save: a changed question set appends a new version, an identical one appends nothing. The form is NOT linked to the template afterwards, so editing the template later never rewrites a live form. The template must belong to the tournament's workspace (else 404 `template_not_found`). The template's game must be the tournament's (else 409 `template_discipline_mismatch`).

rpc.tournament.regform_template_create.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the workspace in the path. Stores a named question set for one game of the workspace (201 Created). `discipline` is required (422 `discipline_required`) and must be enabled for the workspace (422 `discipline_not_enabled`). Names are unique per workspace, case-insensitively: a collision is 409 `template_name_taken` on field `name`.

rpc.tournament.regform_template_delete.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the workspace in the path. Deletes a template by id (204 no body). Nothing references a template -- applying one copies it -- so no tournament form changes.

rpc.tournament.regform_template_list.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.read` on the workspace in the path. Lists that workspace's named registration-form question sets, ordered by name; each carries its game (`discipline`). The optional `discipline` narrows to one game's (422 `discipline_not_installed` for an unknown code).

schema.description: One installed discipline; omitted = every game's templates.

rpc.tournament.regform_template_save_fro.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the tournament's workspace. Snapshots the tournament form's CURRENT question set into a new workspace template under the given name (201 Created). A snapshot, not a link: later edits to either side are invisible to the other. 404 `form_not_configured` when the tournament has no form yet; 409 `template_name_taken` on a case-insensitive name collision. The template takes the tournament's game.

rpc.tournament.regform_template_update.description: Permission: workspace `registration_form.update` on the workspace in the path. Replaces a template's name and question set wholesale. Its game never changes: `discipline` is omitted or equal, another game is 409 `template_discipline_immutable`. 404 `template_not_found` when the id belongs to another workspace; 409 `template_name_taken` on a case-insensitive name collision.

rpc.tournament.regstatus_builtin_reset.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.update` on the workspace in the path. Removes that workspace's override for a built-in registration status (204 no body), reverting to defaults.

rpc.tournament.regstatus_builtin_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.update` on the workspace in the path. Creates or updates a workspace override (icon/color/name/description) for a built-in registration status identified by scope and slug.

rpc.tournament.regstatus_catalog.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.read` on the workspace in the path. Returns the full registration status catalog (built-in plus custom) for that workspace.

rpc.tournament.regstatus_create.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.create` on the workspace in the path. Creates a custom registration status in that workspace (201 Created).

rpc.tournament.regstatus_delete.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.delete` on the workspace in the path. Deletes a custom registration status by id (204 no body).

rpc.tournament.regstatus_list.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.read` on the workspace in the path. Lists that workspace's custom registration statuses.

rpc.tournament.regstatus_update.description: Permission: workspace `registration_status.update` on the workspace in the path. Updates a custom registration status by id.

rpc.tournament.regteam_accept.description: Permission: authenticated user holding the invite — a link invite redeems by its `token` only (by `invite_id` it is 404 `invite_not_found`), a targeted invite by `token` or `invite_id` and only by the account it names (403 otherwise). The body names exactly one of `token` and `invite_id` (422 otherwise). Takes the offered slot, returning the team. A player already registered solo is attached to the team rather than duplicated, and the submitted registration body is then ignored -- their recorded answers stand; a player with no registration yet first passes the tournament's sign-up admission gate (400 when it refuses) and is registered from that body. A player already on another team is never moved: 409 `already_on_team`. A refused accept leaves the invite pending. The consume is a single guarded update, so two simultaneous redemptions of one link cannot both win. 409 on a full slot, a terminal registration, a lost race, or `registration_changed` when the caller's registration changed between the admission check and the team lock.

rpc.tournament.regteam_admission.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Sets the orthogonal admission axis (pending, accepted, waitlisted) without changing occupancy status. Waitlisted complete teams are skipped at export.

rpc.tournament.regteam_attach_admin.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Places a live registration onto a slot, or creates a shadow registration for a BattleTag that has not signed up and places that. Eligibility warnings stay on the team card but do not refuse the write.

rpc.tournament.regteam_check_in.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise). Checks in every approved member except those listed in exclude_registration_ids. Gated by the tournament check-in window. Every member's approval, account and admission are checked in one batch before the team is locked, so a refusal names the first blocked member in roster order; 409 `roster_changed` when the roster changed between that check and the lock.

rpc.tournament.regteam_cover_subscriptio.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise). Stamps the registered team with the captain or manager's active entitlement, or a redeemed challenge code. Only when the form's subscription_scope is team.

rpc.tournament.regteam_create.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller founds the team and is registered as its own captain. Founds a team for a tournament and registers the caller as its captain in one transaction, occupying the requested roster slot. The captain passes the same registration form and the same admission gate as a solo entrant. Returns the new team including its own invites. 400 on an empty name or one containing '#', 409 when the name is taken or the caller is already registered.

rpc.tournament.regteam_decline.description: Permission: authenticated user holding the invite — a link invite is declined by its `token` only (by `invite_id` it is 404 `invite_not_found`), a targeted invite by `token` or `invite_id` and only by the account it names (403 otherwise). The INVITEE refuses an offer made to them, releasing its reserved slot back to the captain (204 no body). The body names exactly one of `token` and `invite_id` (422 otherwise). Distinct from regteam_reject, which is an organizer refusing an entire team. 409 when the invite is no longer pending.

rpc.tournament.regteam_disband.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain (403 for a manager or anyone else). Dissolves their own team (204 no body): members' registrations become withdrawn but keep their team link, so each player's card can say the team was disbanded rather than leaving an unexplained withdrawal, and every pending invite is revoked. The team must still be forming and registration still open. An organizer's equivalent is regteam_reject.

rpc.tournament.regteam_extend_invite.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise); the roster must still be mutable and unlocked. Refreshes a pending invite's TTL. rotate_token is only valid for a link invite and returns a new raw token exactly once.

rpc.tournament.regteam_free_agents.description: Permission: authenticated user; no captaincy, workspace permission or tournament-visibility check is applied. Returns this tournament's live registrants who are on no team, with the roles they signed up for (primary first) -- the picker a captain fills a slot from. Everything here is also on the public participants list. Carries registration ids, never account ids.

rpc.tournament.regteam_image_delete.description: Permission: self-service — that registration team's own captain or team manager, no workspace permission, and only while the team is still forming (mutable and unlocked). Clears a registered team's image URL, commits, then removes its objects from S3; a failed S3 delete is logged and the request still succeeds.

rpc.tournament.regteam_image_upload.description: Permission: self-service — that registration team's own captain or team manager, no workspace permission, and only while the team is still forming (mutable and unlocked). Uploads a registered team's image to S3 and stores its URL. The gateway refuses a multipart body over 5 MiB + 64 KiB (400); an image over 5 MiB or a body that is not valid base64 is 422. The previous image's objects are deleted only after the new URL commits, and a failed cleanup is logged, not an error.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise); no workspace permission substitutes. Offers one roster slot, in either of two modes: with `target_registration_id` it is an in-app offer to a named free agent, which carries no token at all and is read by its recipient through regteam_my_invites; without it a shareable link invite is minted. The link's raw token is returned in this response and nowhere else -- only its sha256 is stored. Expires after `ttl_days` (default 7). The team must still be forming and unlocked, and a pending invite reserves its slot. 409 once the team has issued 60 invites in total, counting revoked and declined ones: revoke an outstanding offer or ask an organizer for a cap reset.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_cap_reset.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Forgives a team's cumulative invite count so its captain can invite again -- the recourse the cap's own 409 names (204 no body). A watermark, not a counter reset: the earlier invites stay readable in the history and only the count's floor moves. 404 when the team belongs to another tournament.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_history.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. Every invite a team ever issued, newest first, with its cumulative cap standing (used, limit, reset watermark) and, per row, whether staff or the captain withdrew it. The same data the team's captain reads through regteam_invite_history_public, which authorizes by captaincy instead.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_history_pu.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers; authorized by team staffing rather than workspace permission. Reads every invite the team ever issued, newest first -- live, accepted, declined, revoked or lapsed -- alongside the cumulative cap standing (used, limit, and the reset watermark if an organizer forgave the count).
