Deliberately still readable after the team is rejected or exported, which is usually when someone opens it. The organizer reads the same data through regteam_invite_history.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_preview.description: Permission: public; no authentication required and no tournament visibility check — the invite token itself is the credential. Resolves a link invite's token to what it offers -- tournament, team, slot, substitute flag, expiry and whether it is still redeemable -- without consuming it. The only anonymous invite surface, so a link into a private tournament still works for its holder. Reveals nothing about the roster. A dead or expired invite answers with its state rather than an error; only a token matching nothing is a 404.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_revoke.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise). Withdraws an outstanding offer the team issued, releasing its reserved slot (204 no body). An organizer reaching into a team they do not captain uses regteam_invite_revoke_admin instead, which records that staff did it. 404 on an unknown invite.

rpc.tournament.regteam_invite_revoke_adm.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. An organizer withdraws an outstanding offer from a team they do not captain (204 no body); the write records that staff did it, which is what distinguishes the row from the captain's own regteam_invite_revoke. Unlike the captain path it does not require the team to still be mutable -- the reason to reach in is usually that something is stuck. The invite must belong to this tournament (404 otherwise, deliberately not 403).

rpc.tournament.regteam_kick.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise). Removes an accepted member, freeing their slot (204 no body). The member's registration survives as withdrawn rather than being deleted. The team must still be forming and unlocked and registration still open; 409 when aimed at the captain themselves -- transfer captaincy or disband instead -- and 404 when the player is not on the team.

rpc.tournament.regteam_leave.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller may only remove their own membership, matched from their own account. A member withdraws themselves from a team, freeing their slot (204 no body); their registration becomes withdrawn. The mirror of regteam_kick. 409 when the caller is the captain -- a captain must transfer or disband rather than vanish from a team others have joined -- and 404 when the caller is not on the team.

rpc.tournament.regteam_list.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. The organizer's view of a tournament's registered teams: every team with its members, its outstanding invites and its per-slot shortfall, plus the number of free agents on no team -- the players the export cannot place. Occupancy is recomputed rather than read off the denormalized status, because the shortfall is what is actionable. `include_terminal` also returns rejected and disbanded teams.

rpc.tournament.regteam_list_public.description: Permission: public; no authentication required beyond the tournament's own visibility rule. The public roster of a tournament's registered teams: name, crest, status, members and each team's remaining per-slot shortfall, plus the count of free agents on no team. Rejected and disbanded teams are omitted, and so are outstanding invites -- except on a team the caller themselves captains or manages, who sees their own pending offers here.

rpc.tournament.regteam_lock.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain (403 for a manager or anyone else). A complete roster can be frozen so further edits refuse with roster_locked until an organizer unlocks it.

rpc.tournament.regteam_my_invites.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the list is scoped to the caller from their own token and there is no id to pass. Returns the targeted invites offered to the calling user in this tournament -- the only way their recipient can learn one exists, since a targeted invite carries no token to paste. Link invites are excluded (a bearer credential has no addressee), as are expired offers and offers from teams no longer forming.

rpc.tournament.regteam_notes.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Staff-only notes on a registered team; never returned on the public roster.
rpc.tournament.regteam_notes.summary: Set organizer notes on a registration team

rpc.tournament.regteam_place_admin.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Moves a live registration onto a slot of a team in this tournament, even from another team. The captain of a source team cannot be moved until captaincy is transferred.
rpc.tournament.regteam_place_admin.summary: Place a player on a registration team (organizer)

rpc.tournament.regteam_place_member.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise); the roster must still be mutable and unlocked. Moves a member to another slot, onto or off the bench, or swaps two members when swap_with_registration_id is set. A captain cannot become a substitute.

rpc.tournament.regteam_reject.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. An ORGANIZER refuses an entire team -- the counterpart of rejecting a solo registration, and distinct from regteam_decline, which is one invitee refusing one offer. Revokes the team's pending invites and returns its members to the solo pool without changing their registration status by default; `withdraw_members: true` explicitly withdraws them instead. Requires a reason of 1–1000 characters after trimming whitespace. The stored reason is visible to the organizer and the entitled captain, including after roster detachment, but not to the public. Returns the rejected team. 404 when the team belongs to another tournament, 409 once it is already exported, rejected or disbanded.

rpc.tournament.regteam_rename.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain or one of its managers (403 otherwise). Renames their team. The roster must still be mutable and unlocked. '#' in a name is refused.

rpc.tournament.regteam_rename_admin.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. An organizer renames a registered team they do not captain. 404 when the team belongs to another tournament (deliberately not 403).

rpc.tournament.regteam_set_manager.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain (403 for a manager or anyone else); the roster must still be mutable and unlocked. Flags another accepted member as a manager so they can invite, kick, rename and check the roster in. The captain themselves is not a manager.

rpc.tournament.regteam_transfer_captain.description: Permission: authenticated user who is the team's own captain (403 for a manager or anyone else). Hands captaincy to another accepted member (204 no body); the roster itself is unchanged. The team must still be forming and registration still open. 404 when the successor is not on the team, 409 when they are a substitute -- a bench player holds no starter slot and cannot captain the roster.

rpc.tournament.regteam_unlock.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the tournament's workspace. Clears a captain's roster lock so the team can edit again. Organizer-only; captains lock, they do not unlock.

rpc.tournament.report_form_get.description: Permission: workspace `match.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns the tournament's captain match-report form config: which built-in fields (closeness, map codes, comment) are enabled and required, plus any organizer-defined text fields. Always a complete config — a tournament that has never been configured answers the defaults rather than null.

rpc.tournament.report_form_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `match.update` on the tournament's workspace. Creates or replaces the tournament's captain match-report form config. Custom fields are text only, capped at 20, and their keys must be unique, slug-shaped and not collide with a built-in field name (422 otherwise). Rules apply to new submissions only; existing reports stay valid and readable.

rpc.tournament.saved_view_create.description: Permission: authenticated member of the workspace named by `workspace_id` (403 otherwise); self-service — the view belongs to the caller. Creates the calling user's saved encounter filter view in a workspace; 409 `saved_view_exists` when the caller already has a view of that name, 409 `saved_view_limit` when the caller already keeps 20 views there.

rpc.tournament.saved_view_delete.description: Permission: authenticated member of the workspace named by `workspace_id` (403 otherwise); self-service — only the caller's own view is deleted. Deletes the calling user's saved encounter view by id in a workspace (204 no body).

rpc.tournament.saved_views.description: Permission: any authenticated caller, self-service — only the caller's own views are returned (401 without an identity). Returns the calling user's saved encounter filter views for the workspace.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.

rpc.tournament.scrim_claim.description: Permission: authenticated member of the room's workspace plus the room's share token (membership only — no resource grant is checked). Claims the scrim room's free captain side for the calling user and grants them preview access to the hidden scrims container, so the pre-game room resolves their side from then on; idempotent and first-writer-wins, 409 once both sides are taken.

rpc.tournament.scrim_close.description: Permission: self-service — the room's creator, a captain of either side, a superuser, or workspace staff holding `match.result` (plain workspace membership is not enough). Closes a scrim room so it stops counting against its creator's active-room cap, leaving the encounter and its pick-ban history readable by the participants forever. The same rule is surfaced per room as `can_close`.

rpc.tournament.scrim_create.description: Permission: authenticated user who is a member of the target workspace (membership only — no resource grant is checked; superusers pass). Creates an ad-hoc pre-game room outside any tournament: the workspace's hidden scrims container (lazily), an isolating stage, that stage's map and optional hero pick-ban configs either copied from an existing tournament round or authored ad hoc, both teams and the encounter; returns the room with its share token. 409s when the caller's active-room cap is reached.

rpc.tournament.scrim_get.description: Permission: authentication optional — the room is gated by the ordinary visibility rules of its hidden scrims container, not by holding the token. Returns one scrim room by share token, annotating the requesting viewer's captain side and whether they may still claim the free one; visible only to a participant, a workspace insider or a preview-allowlisted user, everyone else gets 404.

rpc.tournament.scrim_list_mine.description: Permission: authenticated user who is a member of the queried workspace (membership only — no resource grant is checked), plus workspace `match.result` when `scope=workspace`; 401 without an identity. Returns the calling user's scrim rooms in a workspace, open and closed alike (scrim history is kept forever); `scope=workspace` instead returns every room of the workspace so staff can find one they neither created nor play, same open-first ordering.

rpc.tournament.sheet_get.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns a tournament's registration Google Sheets feed config, or null if none.

rpc.tournament.sheet_mapping_catalog.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns the available registration field mapping catalog (optionally with sheet headers).

rpc.tournament.sheet_players_export.description: Permission: workspace `player.read` on the tournament's workspace. Exports a tournament's balancer pool as a players payload. `format=xv-1` (default) is the solver's own input contract, accepted as-is by the balance-job upload. `format=owt-1` is the full snapshot: the same player nodes plus per-player `owt` metadata (identity ids, every declared role with its rank source, division and top heroes, workflow status) and the tournament's roster shape including flex slots. `include_private=1` adds the organizer-only block (notes, admin notes, custom-field answers, contacts, smurf tags). Metered: a 429 reports `code=rate_limited` with the exceeded limit in `details.limit_name`.

schema.description: xv-1 (solver input, default) or owt-1 (full snapshot)
owt-1 only: add notes, admin notes, custom fields and contacts

rpc.tournament.sheet_preview.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. Previews how sample sheet rows map to registrations under the given mapping config.

rpc.tournament.sheet_suggest_mapping.description: Permission: workspace `team.read` on the tournament's workspace. Reads a source sheet and suggests a column-to-field mapping with detected headers.

rpc.tournament.sheet_sync.description: Permission: workspace `team.create` on the tournament's workspace. Syncs registrations from the configured Google Sheet and returns created/updated/withdrawn/skipped counts plus errors. Only rows whose content changed since the last sync are re-applied and counted in `updated`; a sync that changed nothing sends no invalidation, and ranks the sheet does not map are kept. While another sync of the same feed runs (the scheduler's or another request's), it returns zero counts without syncing. Metered: a 429 reports `code=rate_limited` with the exceeded limit in `details.limit_name`.

rpc.tournament.sheet_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `team.create` on the tournament's workspace. Creates or updates a tournament's registration Google Sheets feed config.

rpc.tournament.stage_activate.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Activates a stage.

rpc.tournament.stage_activate_and_genera.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace (the optional force flag needs no extra grant). Enqueues a combined activate-and-generate bracket job (202 Accepted), honoring an optional force flag.

rpc.tournament.stage_apply_best_of.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Rewrites best_of on the stage's existing encounters from the stage's best-of config (in place, preserving scores).

rpc.tournament.stage_auto_wire.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Wires the stage's TENTATIVE inputs from a round-robin/Swiss stage's "Teams advancing to playoff" count — the same auto-wire Activate & generate runs automatically, exposed standalone for preview/debugging. The source is the one group stage of the latest earlier phase; pass source_stage_id to name it when that phase runs several divisions in parallel (a value that is not an integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`).

schema.description: The group stage to wire from.

rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_preview.description: Permission: workspace `stage.read` on the stage's workspace. Returns the bracket a stage would generate — the real generator's pairings, seed order, advancement edges and per-round best-of, with skeleton-local ids because nothing is written; wired teams appear by name, an unseeded playoff is projected from the preceding group stage.

rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_preview_pub.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — a hidden tournament is visible only to its workspace's admins and users on its preview allowlist, and a stage of another tournament is a 404. The same read-only skeleton as the admin bracket preview, for drawing an elimination stage whose matches are not generated yet.

rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_template_cl.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update`. Drops the custom template; refused with 409 while the stage has matches.
rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_template_cl.summary: Reset to the generated bracket layout

rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_template_ge.description: Permission: workspace `stage.read`. The stage's custom bracket template, or the one its format would generate for the current seed counts, plus those counts.

rpc.tournament.stage_bracket_template_se.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update`. Validates the template (spec rules) and stores it; refused with 409 while the stage has matches. An invalid template is a 422 whose `details.fields[0]` carries `code: "invalid_bracket_template"` plus a `problems` array of `{match_id, slot, code, message}`.

rpc.tournament.stage_deactivate.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Reverts an accidentally-activated stage back to Draft/preview; refuses (409) once any of its matches has been reported or started.

rpc.tournament.stage_generate.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Enqueues a bracket-generation job (202 Accepted) for the stage.

rpc.tournament.stage_merge.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the target stage's workspace. Merges source group stages into a target stage.

rpc.tournament.stage_planned_rounds.description: Permission: workspace `stage.read` on the stage's workspace. Returns the round numbers a stage's bracket has (once generated) or will have, predicted from its planned team inputs.

rpc.tournament.stage_progress.description: Permission: workspace `stage.read` on the tournament's workspace. Returns per-stage progress for a tournament.

rpc.tournament.stage_seed.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the stage's workspace. Seeds the given teams into a stage using the requested mode. Takes the stage's row lock like every other stage writer; 409 when the stage already has generated matches (delete them first to edit the bracket).

rpc.tournament.stage_wire.description: Permission: workspace `stage.update` on the target stage's workspace. Wires a target stage's slots from a source group stage's top placements.

rpc.tournament.standing_pins_set.description: Permission: workspace `standing.update` on the stage's workspace. Replaces every pin of one standings table (the stage plus body `stage_item_id`, null for an elimination stage): a pinned team keeps that place whatever results arrive later, the others fill the free places in computed order. An empty `pins` list unpins the table. 422 for a team outside the table or a place past its end; 409 when a playoff seeded from the group is under way and the change touches its qualifying places or removes a pin. Schedules the standings-recalculation job that applies them (202 Accepted).

rpc.tournament.standing_recalculate.description: Permission: workspace `standing.update` on the tournament's workspace. Schedules a durable standings-recalculation job (202 Accepted) for the tournament.

rpc.tournament.statistics_division.description: Permission: public; no authentication required. Returns, for the tournaments of the game named by the required `discipline` query param (422 when absent, 404 `discipline_not_installed` for an unknown code), the average division per tournament keyed by the top-level role codes of that game's rated dimension (`role_avg_divs`; a role nobody played is absent), normalized against the workspace's division grid for that game with fallback to its global grid. Hidden tournaments and the tournaments of hidden workspaces are left out.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.
Explicit discipline code.

rpc.tournament.statistics_history.description: Permission: public; no authentication required. Returns per-tournament historical statistics for the workspace; hidden tournaments and the tournaments of hidden workspaces are left out.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.

rpc.tournament.statistics_overall.description: Permission: public; no authentication required. Returns aggregate tournament statistics across the workspace: counts of tournaments, teams, players and champions, plus played volume — finished encounters, maps, distinct calendar days covered (overlapping tournaments counted once) and whole hours of logged map time.

schema.description: Workspace id; `all` is the same as absent. Any other non-integer is 422 `invalid_query_param`.

rpc.tournament.sub_config_list.description: Permission: workspace `subscription.read` on the workspace in the path. Returns every configurable subscription provider for that workspace (present or not) with its raw ids; challenge codes are redacted to tier and expiry only.

rpc.tournament.sub_config_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `subscription.update` on the workspace in the path. Creates or updates one provider's config (Discord guild id and role→tier mapping, Twitch broadcaster, challenge codes) and its verification_method: 'live' accepts only the provider's own signal, 'code' only a redeemed challenge code, 'any' either. Narrowing the method revokes stored entitlements whose source it no longer accepts. Plaintext codes are hashed server-side and never stored; omitting a field keeps the stored value.

rpc.tournament.sub_me.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the caller's own subscription standing only. Returns the calling user's composed subscription outcome for the tournament plus a per-provider verdict; never forces a provider refresh.

rpc.tournament.sub_redeem_code.description: Permission: authenticated user; self-service — the entitlement is granted to the caller's own account. Redeems a challenge code published in a subscriber-only post, granting an entitlement at the code's tier; never downgrades an existing higher tier and is rate-limited per user.

rpc.tournament.sub_requirement_get.description: Permission: workspace `subscription.read` on the workspace in the path. Returns the workspace's subscription admission rule as `{mode, requirements: [{provider, min_tier_rank}]}`, shared by every tournament in the workspace whose registration form has require_subscription on; an empty object means nothing is enforced.

rpc.tournament.sub_requirement_upsert.description: Permission: workspace `subscription.update` on the workspace in the path. Replaces the workspace's admission rule wholesale (no partial merge -- that would be a silent policy change). `mode` is 'all' or 'any'; each row names a provider and its min_tier_rank. An unknown mode or a row without a provider is rejected with 422 rather than degrading at check-in. An empty `requirements` list clears the rule, which disarms every tournament in the workspace whose toggle is on.

rpc.tournament.team_format.get.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.read`. The tournament's own team format with its slot projection.

rpc.tournament.team_format.put.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.update`. Replaces the tournament's team format; 409 while a draft is unfinished or teams hold slots; 422 with the `team_format_*` code when the format cannot be stored.

rpc.tournament.teams.image_delete.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the workspace resolved from the team's tournament. Clears a team's image URL, commits, then removes its objects from S3; a failed S3 delete is logged and the request still succeeds.

rpc.tournament.teams.image_upload.description: Permission: workspace `team.update` on the workspace resolved from the team's tournament. Uploads a team's image to S3 and stores its URL. The gateway refuses a multipart body over 5 MiB + 64 KiB (400); an image over 5 MiB or a body that is not valid base64 is 422. The previous image's objects are deleted only after the new URL commits, and a failed cleanup is logged, not an error.

rpc.tournament.tournament_finish.description: Permission: superuser only. Toggles a tournament's `is_finished` flag and returns it with stages.

rpc.tournament.tournament_readiness.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.read` or `team.read` on the tournament's own workspace. Returns the living readiness checklist for one tournament, telling its organisers what is still missing before it can run: schedule/grid/stage-slot configuration, bracket, duel log coverage and pending standings recalculation (`tournament.read`); the registration, pool, balance and draft state (`team.read`); the overdue, pending-confirmation and disputed results (`match.read`); and the achievement evaluation status (`achievement.read`). Each group of fields is masked to null when the caller lacks the permission that gates it, so a partial reader sees no-access rather than zeros. 403 without `tournament.read` or `team.read`, 404 if the tournament is unknown; hidden tournaments of the caller's own workspace are visible.

rpc.tournament.tournament_schedule_set.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.update` on the tournament's workspace. Replaces the tournament's phase schedule (full replace of REGISTRATION/CHECK_IN/DRAFT/LIVE rows).

rpc.tournament.tournament_status.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.update` on the tournament's workspace; the `force` flag additionally requires superuser. Transitions a tournament to the requested status.

rpc.tournament.tournaments.image_delete.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.update` on the tournament's workspace. Clears a tournament's cover or logo URL, commits, then removes its objects from S3; the slot path segment is 'cover' or 'logo'. A failed S3 delete is logged and the request still succeeds. Answers the tournament with `stages`, `roster_shape`, `division_grid_version` and `rules`.

rpc.tournament.tournaments.image_upload.description: Permission: workspace `tournament.update` on the tournament's workspace. Uploads a tournament's cover or logo to S3 and stores its URL; the slot path segment is 'cover' or 'logo'. The gateway refuses a multipart body over 5 MiB + 64 KiB (400); an image over 5 MiB or a body that is not valid base64 is 422. The previous image's objects are deleted only after the new URL commits, and a failed cleanup is logged, not an error. Answers the tournament with `stages`, `roster_shape`, `division_grid_version` and `rules`.

rpc.tournament.tournaments_facets.description: Permission: public; no authentication required — every count is filtered to the tournaments the viewer may see. Returns chip counters for the tournaments list: unfiltered total/live plus per-status and league/standard counts, each axis counted without its own filter.

Request schema for the synchronous, stateless balance (``rpc.balancer.balance``).

Everything the solver needs travels in this payload: the pool, the per-team
roster shape and the knobs. Nothing is read from the workspace, so the same
body balanced twice yields the same teams regardless of tournament state.

knob on a request whose whole point is being self-describing.

crossover_rate.description: Probability of crossover when producing offspring in the Rust MOO search.

generation_count.description: Maximum optimization iterations. Higher values can improve quality and increase runtime.

greedy_seed_count.description: How many initial individuals are built with greedy seeding before random fill.
greedy_seed_count.title: Greedy Seed Count

internal_role_spread_weight.description: Penalty weight for uneven average strength between roles inside the same team.
internal_role_spread_weight.title: Internal Role Spread Weight

intra_team_std_weight.description: Weight for the standard deviation of ratings inside each team. Higher values push the optimizer to spread top players across teams.
intra_team_std_weight.title: Intra Team Std Weight

island_count.description: Number of independent Rust MOO islands explored in parallel before merging the archive.
island_count.title: Island Count

low_rank_collision_weight.description: Penalty weight per pair of low-rank players in the same team, normalized per team count. Discourages stacking two low-rank players together.
low_rank_collision_weight.title: Low Rank Collision Weight

low_rank_threshold.description: Players whose best role rating is at or below this value (canonical scale, see rating_scale_ceiling) count as low-rank; teams with two or more of them get penalized. 0 disables the mechanic.

max_result_variants.description: Maximum number of solution variants returned by the selected solver.
max_result_variants.title: Max Result Variants

max_role_discomfort_weight.description: Penalty weight for the single worst role discomfort assignment in a solution.
max_role_discomfort_weight.title: Max Role Discomfort Weight

max_team_gap_weight.description: Penalty weight for the rating gap between the strongest and weakest teams.
max_team_gap_weight.title: Max Team Gap Weight

mix_comfort_tilt.description: Mix trade-off between rank balance and role comfort. 0 weighs only how evenly the two teams' ranks split, 1 only how many players got a preferred role; 0.5 reproduces the engine's own defaults.
mix_comfort_tilt.title: Mix Comfort Tilt

mutation_rate.description: Probability that a solution is changed while producing the next generation.
mutation_rate.title: Mutation Rate

mutation_rate_max.description: Upper bound for the adaptive mutation rate during Rust MOO search.
mutation_rate_max.title: Mutation Rate Max

mutation_rate_min.description: Lower bound for the adaptive mutation rate during Rust MOO search.
mutation_rate_min.title: Mutation Rate Min

mutation_strength.description: Number of swap/change operations attempted during a mutation.
mutation_strength.title: Mutation Strength

open_slot_settings.description: Weights of open slots without a role constraint.

polish_max_passes.description: Maximum local-improvement passes applied to each archive solution after the main search.
polish_max_passes.title: Polish Max Passes

population_size.description: Number of candidate balances kept per generation. Higher values improve search coverage and cost more time.
population_size.title: Population Size

rank_comfort_tilt.description: Shifts how result variants are ranked: 0.5 weighs team balance (StdDev) and comfort (off-role) equally; toward 1 prioritises comfort/off-role, toward 0 prioritises balance. Ordering and primary selection only — does not change the optimizer search.
rank_comfort_tilt.title: Rank Comfort Tilt

role_discomfort_weight.description: Penalty weight for assigning players away from their preferred roles.
role_discomfort_weight.title: Role Discomfort Weight

role_line_balance_weight.description: Penalty weight for uneven rating strength between the same role across teams.
role_line_balance_weight.title: Role Line Balance Weight

role_settings.description: Per-role weights keyed by roster slot code: how much a role counts towards a team's effective total, and how hard uneven lines of it are penalized.

stagnation_kick_patience.description: Generations without archive improvement before stronger mutation and crossover are applied.

sub_role_collision_weight.description: Penalty weight per pair of players in the same team sharing the same role subclass, normalized per team count. Use 0 to disable.
sub_role_collision_weight.title: Sub Role Collision Weight

team_max_pain_weight.description: Penalty weight for the per-team maximum role discomfort averaged over all teams. Makes 'one suffering player in every team' visible, unlike the single global maximum.

form's own validation downstream. ``None`` rather than an empty default: a
submission carries the ``form_version_id`` it answered, and there is no honest

captainless team to exist between the two calls.

tournament.RegistrationTeamDeclineReques.description:

targeted one is not, the ambiguity is a privilege question, not a cosmetic one.

tournament; omitting it produces a shareable link for someone with no account
yet. Both modes are one entity, so the slot accounting cannot
diverge between them.

A REGISTRATION id, not an account id: the captain picks from this tournament's
own free agents, so no global account search — and no new identity surface —
is needed. The server resolves the account behind it and stores that, because
identity is what an invite is bound to; a registration can be withdrawn and
resubmitted underneath it.

reserves roster slots. Terminal rows must never appear there — a declined offer
holding a place is the bug that separation prevents.

live list shows only pending ones; without the history a captain refused at
the ceiling cannot see where the cap went.

question for a LINK held by a stranger. This one is for a targeted invite,
which has no token at all — so this read is the only way its recipient can
ever learn it exists.
tournament.RegistrationTeamInviteOffer.title: RegistrationTeamInviteOffer

tournament.RegistrationTeamInvitePreview.description:
What a link invite reveals BEFORE it is redeemed.

Deliberately minimal: the holder of a token is not yet a member, so this shows
what they are being asked to join and nothing about who else is on the roster.
It carries ``state`` rather than 404-ing a dead invite, so the landing page can
say *why* a link no longer works instead of looking broken.
tournament.RegistrationTeamInvitePreview.title: RegistrationTeamInvitePreview

tournament.RegistrationUpdate.description: A partial edit: only the keys present in ``answers`` are validated and written.
tournament.RegistrationUpdate.title: RegistrationUpdate

tournament.ReopenResultIn.description:
Body of the result reopen: the organizer's stated reason.

Reopening unmakes a human decision, so a human signs it -- the journal row
``reopen`` writes carries this verbatim.
tournament.ReopenResultIn.title: ReopenResultIn

tournament.ReplayCodeRead.description:
One participation's replay code for one position (``game_team.replay_code``).

``encounter_team_id`` is the participation; its slot comes from the row's
``participations``.
tournament.ReplayCodeRead.title: ReplayCodeRead

tournament.RoleRef.description: ``role`` is the leaf an assignment names; ``parent`` is derived and ignored on input.
tournament.RoleRef.title: RoleRef

tournament.RoleTierUpsert.description:
One ``discord role -> subscription tier`` mapping.

``role_id`` is a string because a Discord snowflake exceeds 2**53 and must
never survive a float round-trip.
tournament.RoleTierUpsert.title: RoleTierUpsert

tournament.RosterShapeRead.description: A team format's slots. The frontend never recomputes them.
tournament.RosterShapeRead.title: RosterShapeRead

tournament.ScoringColumnRead.description: ``ScoringColumnSettings`` as stored: read back without the write-time checks.
tournament.ScoringColumnRead.title: ScoringColumnRead

tournament.ScoringColumnSettings.description: One value a stage's games record per team.
tournament.ScoringColumnSettings.title: ScoringColumnSettings

tournament.ScrimPoolCopy.description:
"We play this round's maps" — clone whatever the cascade resolves there.

``stage_id``/``round`` may be null to copy a tournament-wide or stage-wide
config; resolution uses the engine's own ranking
(``pick_ban_session.resolve_config_at_level``), so what a room copies is
exactly what an encounter at that coordinate would have played.
tournament.ScrimPoolCopy.title: ScrimPoolCopy

tournament.ScrimPoolCustom.description: A pool authored for this room only. At most one entry per ``kind``.
tournament.ScrimPoolCustom.title: ScrimPoolCustom

tournament.ScrimPoolSlotInput.description:
One slot of a slot-mode pool. List order IS play order — same contract as
``PickBanConfigSlotUpsert``.
tournament.ScrimPoolSlotInput.title: ScrimPoolSlotInput

tournament.SeedTeamsRequest.description:
Distribute teams into a stage's stage_items (groups) automatically.

``mode`` selects the distribution strategy:
- ``snake_sr`` (default) — sort by Team.avg_sr desc, snake-distribute
  across groups so each group ends up roughly equally strong.
- ``by_total_sr`` — same but sorts by Team.total_sr (raw sum).
- ``random`` — deterministic shuffle based on team.id (reproducible).
tournament.SeedTeamsRequest.title: SeedTeamsRequest

tournament.SetResultIn.description:
Body of the single admin result write.

``reason`` is required: an admin result overrides what the participants
said and the journal has to say why. ``results`` may be empty only when
``adopt_report_team_id`` names the participation whose report is taken as
truth instead -- which is how a dispute is resolved in one call.
tournament.SetResultIn.title: SetResultIn

tournament.SetResultLineIn.description: One participation's line of an admin result.
tournament.SetResultLineIn.title: SetResultLineIn

tournament.StageBestOf.description:
Series length per encounter: ``final`` (an elimination stage's last round),
a Swiss decisive match's ``swiss_qualify`` / ``swiss_eliminate`` (the larger
when it is both), else the round's own ``by_round`` entry, else ``default``.
tournament.StageBestOf.title: StageBestOf

tournament.StageScoring.description:
How a stage scores, at all three levels.

``win``/``draw``/``loss`` are level 3: what one encounter's result pays in
the stage table; ``None`` = the tournament's points. The rest is the
``encounter.scoring_rule`` every encounter of the stage is played and
ranked by -- ``wins`` is a Bo-N series, ``points`` a lobby scored by the
organizer's own columns.

Every rule field is nullable and means "the preset's default", the way
``ranking_preset`` does: the preset itself defaults to the one the stage
TYPE implies, which only the service knows.
tournament.StageScoring.title: StageScoring

tournament.StageScoringRead.description:
``StageScoring`` as stored, without its write validators.

A read reports the rule the stage was saved with; re-validating it would recompile the formula on every stage
read, and a rule saved before the formula language reserved another name would 422 every list that embeds it.
tournament.StageScoringRead.title: StageScoringRead

tournament.StageUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change (the service reads
``exclude_unset``). ``scoring`` and ``best_of`` are each replaced as a
whole. The non-nullable regulation fields carry a default only
so that an explicit ``null`` is refused instead of written.
tournament.StageUpdate.title: StageUpdate

tournament.StandingPinsUpdate.description:
Every pin one standings table should have, replacing what it had.

The table is the stage from the path plus ``stage_item_id`` (its group; NULL
for an elimination stage, whose table spans the whole stage). An empty
``pins`` list unpins the whole table.
tournament.StandingPinsUpdate.title: StandingPinsUpdate

tournament.SubscriptionEnforcementStage.description:
The EARLIEST admission gate a subscription requirement blocks at.

Ordered, not a set: ``registration`` implies check-in too. Requiring a
subscription to sign up while admitting an unsubscribed player at check-in
would be incoherent, so there is no "registration only" value to pick wrongly.

Off is not a member -- that is ``registration_form.require_subscription``
being false. Same shape as ``require_open_profile`` + ``open_profile_scope``
in the same table: one flag for whether, one value for how.
tournament.SubscriptionEnforcementStage.title: SubscriptionEnforcementStage

tournament.SubscriptionProviderConfigUps.description:
Per-workspace provider setup.

Every field except ``provider``/``enabled`` is optional and OMITTING it keeps
whatever is stored. That matters most for ``codes``: the admin never sees the
existing ones (only digests are kept), so a plain save must not wipe them.
Passing an explicit list replaces them.
tournament.SubscriptionProviderConfigUps.title: SubscriptionProviderConfigUpsert

tournament.SubscriptionProviderVerdictRe.description:
One provider's verdict, as shown to the patron.

Deliberately narrow: ``evidence`` may hold guild ids and role ids, so only
``reason`` is exposed -- the UI branches on it to pick a call to action
("link Discord" vs "reconnect Twitch").
tournament.SubscriptionProviderVerdictRe.title: SubscriptionProviderVerdictRead

tournament.SubscriptionRedeemRequest.description:
Body of the challenge-code redemption endpoint.

``provider`` defaults to ``boosty`` because the challenge code exists
specifically for it -- Twitch has a real API and needs no code.
tournament.SubscriptionRedeemRequest.title: SubscriptionRedeemRequest

tournament.SubscriptionStatusRead.description:
The caller's own subscription standing for one tournament.

``outcome`` is the COMPOSED answer over the tournament's requirement;
``verdicts`` is per provider so the form can render a chip per account row.
``required`` is false when the tournament does not gate on a subscription, in
which case the rest is informational only.
tournament.SubscriptionStatusRead.title: SubscriptionStatusRead

tournament.TeamGroupRead.description: The group a team played in: a ``StageItem`` of type GROUP, name only.
tournament.TeamGroupRead.title: TeamGroupRead

tournament.TeamReportIn.description:
One participation's independent report of the finished encounter.

``results`` carries one line per live seat -- a duel reports two, a lobby
as many as it seats, and neither is oriented. Everything after
``games_played`` is optional here and validated against the tournament's
report-form config server-side (``services.encounter.report_form``),
because what is required depends on that config, not on the wire shape.
tournament.TeamReportIn.title: TeamReportIn

tournament.TeamReportRead.description: One participation's independent report of an encounter's result.
tournament.TeamReportRead.title: TeamReportRead

tournament.TeamReportResultIn.description:
One participation's line of a series report.

``wins`` is omitted when the encounter's rule does not count them (a
lobby's card, where points alone decide); ``placement`` when the form does
not ask for places.
tournament.TeamReportResultIn.title: TeamReportResultIn

tournament.TeamReportResultRead.description: One participation's line inside one report.
tournament.TeamReportResultRead.title: TeamReportResultRead

tournament.TournamentFacets.description:
Chip counters for the public tournaments page.

``total``/``live`` are unconditional platform facts (see
``TournamentFlowsService.get_facets``); ``by_status`` and ``league``/
``standard`` each ignore their own filter so a selected chip never zeroes its
siblings.
tournament.TournamentFacets.title: TournamentFacets

tournament.TournamentFacetsQueryParams.description:
Query model for ``rpc.tournament.tournaments_facets``.

The same filter axes ``TournamentPaginationSortSearchQueryParams`` carries,
minus pagination and sorting: counting a facet consumes no page.
tournament.TournamentFacetsQueryParams.title: TournamentFacetsQueryParams

tournament.TournamentPhaseScheduleRead.description: One phase-schedule row: when phase ``status`` starts (and its action window ends).
tournament.TournamentPhaseScheduleRead.title: TournamentPhaseScheduleRead

tournament.TournamentReadiness.description:
Living-checklist aggregate for one tournament.

Field groups are masked by the caller's workspace permissions:
``tournament.read`` gates the setup/bracket/logs/recalc fields, ``team.read``
the registration/pool/balance/draft fields, ``match.read`` the result backlog
and ``achievement.read`` the evaluation status — a missing group yields
``None`` so the checklist renders "no-access" instead of zeros.
tournament.TournamentReadiness.title: TournamentReadiness

tournament.TournamentScheduleEntryInput.description: One phase-schedule row in a full-replace schedule update.
tournament.TournamentScheduleEntryInput.title: TournamentScheduleEntryInput

tournament.TournamentScheduleSet.description: A tournament's whole phase schedule; replaces the stored one.
tournament.TournamentScheduleSet.title: TournamentScheduleSet

tournament.WireFromGroupsRequest.description:
Auto-wire TENTATIVE inputs in a playoff stage from a group stage.

``top`` = number of teams per group going to the upper bracket (UB).
``top_lb`` = number of teams per group going to the lower bracket (LB).
When ``top_lb=0`` (default) all teams go into the UB item only.

Total UB slots = num_groups * top; total LB slots = num_groups * top_lb.
LB positions start from ``top + 1`` in each group's standings.

``mode`` = seeding pattern. "cross" avoids same-group rematches in R1
by alternating direction per column; "snake" does plain top-down.
tournament.WireFromGroupsRequest.title: WireFromGroupsRequest

tournament.WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirem.description:
The rule a whole workspace enforces, shared by every tournament in it.

``requirement`` is the raw ``{mode, requirements: [{provider, min_tier_rank}]}``
blob rather than a nested model on purpose: ``parse_requirement`` is the single
authority on that shape (it clamps thresholds and keeps the strictest duplicate),
and a second Pydantic definition of it would be a second source of truth for the
admission rule.
tournament.WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirem.title: WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirementRead

tournament.WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirem.description:
Replaces the rule wholesale -- a partial merge of an admission rule would be
a silent policy change, and an empty ``requirements`` list is the way to clear it.
tournament.WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirem.title: WorkspaceSubscriptionRequirementUpsert
